[MUQATIL:82:6-13/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | God assembled the human in whatever form He willed; He could have made him in a form other than human.
[AKHFASH:v2p570/r3] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | holds | The adjacent identical kāf consonants may assimilate; he also describes when to leave them unassimilated according to whether the first or second letter is vowelled.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r4] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | Kallā in the next clause means matters are not as the addressee has deluded himself.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r4] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · قوم | rejects | Some read the verse as transmigration of souls, but Ibn Qutayba rejects that reading and says the address is not to one particular person.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r5] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | The address is generic, as in O human, striving toward your Lord; God formed and proportioned people in whatever forms He chose, in beauty, ugliness, whiteness, blackness, dark complexion, or redness. | mentions 84:6, 30:22
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r6] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | He links the variety of chosen human forms and colors to the signs in the creation of the heavens and earth and the variation of human languages and colors. | mentions 30:22
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p70/r7] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · قوم | reports | Some say God's utterance is not real speech but the production of meanings, and treat much Quranic speech metaphorically, like saying a wall spoke when it leaned.
[TAB-FULL:v24p178/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says God formed the human in the likeness of a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
[TAB-FULL:v24p178/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · إسماعيل عن سفيان | reports | Ismail reports that God could form a person in a dog's or donkey's image if He willed.
[TAB-FULL:v24p178/r7] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · أبو صالح | reports | Abu Salih gives the possible images as a pig or a donkey.
[TAB-FULL:v24p178/r8] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عكرمة | reports | Ikrima says God could form a person as a monkey or a pig.
[TAB-FULL:v24p178/r9] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet tells a questioner that, once semen settles in the womb, God brings forth every lineage between it and Adam, so resemblance may be to either parent; he invokes this verse.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p295#2/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | reports | If mā is an emphatic extra particle, the sense is that God formed you in whichever shape He wished, tall or short, attractive or otherwise.
[ZAJJAJ:v5p295#2/r2] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | reports | Alternatively, mā is conditional: in whatever shape He chose to form you, He formed you in it.
[NAHHAS:v5p169/r2] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | ما is extra in the construction.
[NAHHAS:v5p169/r3] NAHHAS, d. 338 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says God formed the person in the image of a father, mother, uncle, or maternal uncle.
[THALABI:v10p147#2/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | In a report about a child’s resemblance, the Prophet says that once semen settles in the womb God brings the lineages back to Adam and may form the child as a human, donkey, monkey, dog, or pig.
[THALABI:v10p147/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says the chosen resemblance may come from a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r11] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | God fitted the body's limbs according to wise designs, varying beauty and ugliness, and height and shortness.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r12] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | Alternatively, “image” means attribute and fī means ʿalā; God formed each person in the attribute He willed, whether felicity or misery, faith or disobedience.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء والزجاج | reports | Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj say the image may be tall, short, handsome, or otherwise; on their reading, ما is an emphatic extra particle.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء والزجاج | reports | In al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj's explanation, ما in ما شاء is an additional particle used for emphasis.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل | reports | Muqātil, also joined by Abū Ṣāliḥ, says God could have formed the person in a nonhuman shape such as a dog, donkey, pig, or ape.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abū Isḥāq parses ما conditionally: in whatever form God wills to form the person, He forms him in it.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid takes the image to mean the form of a father, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p296/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · النبي | reports | A report from the Prophet says that once the sperm settles in the womb, God brings forth every lineage between it and Adam; al-Wāḥidī cites it as support for Mujāhid's view, without grading it.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:8-19/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | God composed each person in the form He willed, whether tall or short, handsome or ugly.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r1] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | In representation (tamthīl), one image appears as a single image seen first in a mirror and then directly; explicit simile presents two actual images.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r2] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Abstract nearness and distance require a sensory model: a man can be distant in status yet near in generosity only by recalling the moon’s physical distance and near light.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r3] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Visible qualities of a flower can be perceived directly, without simile; comparison adds a second image to the one already seen.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p206/r4] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | In the abstract comparison, the branch does not possess the original’s actual quality; it only seems present, like a second person in a mirror that vanishes when the correspondence ends.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r1] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | The paired-sun poem aims to astonish listeners with an event outside experience and ordinary custom.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r2] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | To sustain that wonder, the poet boldly asserts the impossible as fact, disregarding expected denial and the appearance of falsehood.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r3] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | The sun-shading, two-suns, and other poems share only the broad device of asserting an impossible sight; their distinct specific wonders mean this shared idea is not plagiarism.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r4] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Al-Mutanabbī’s image of suns appearing from the beloveds’ homes without an east is a distinct version of the impossible-sun conceit.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r5] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Another distinct wonder has the moon walk toward a person and lions embrace a man; the marvel lies in those specific violations of ordinary experience.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p264/r6] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | A reverse technique assigns a subtle, distinctive feature of the comparison’s source to the target, making the simile or metaphor seem to disappear.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r1] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | A true metaphor works like a genuine loan: the borrowed name must confer its full use on the recipient, as clothing is lent for the borrower to wear as its owner would.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r2] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | In “Zayd is a lion,” the name Zayd prevents lion from applying to him with the unrestricted force of its literal name; this is unlike a complete transfer of the noun.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p281/r3] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | With “I meant a gazelle,” the noun is understood in its ordinary animal sense, not as naming a woman; Jurjānī uses this to show what unrestricted application of a name entails.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r1] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Figurative attribution does more than assign a property to an undeserving branch: the comparison implicitly attributes it to the rightful original as well.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r2] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | A man can be likened to a lion in courage only by first recognizing courage as one of the lion’s most characteristic and predominant qualities.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r3] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Attributing an action to a cause presupposes the rational principle that real action belongs to a capable agent; without that basis, the causal assertion would be literal rather than figurative.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r4] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | rejects | Jurjānī excludes the disbelievers’ literal claim that time alone destroys from his discussion of figurative causal attribution. | mentions 45:24
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r5] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Saying that a knife cuts or a sword kills only forms a coherent attribution when the listener also imagines the actual agent wielding the instrument.
[JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p335/r6] JURJANI-ASRAR, d. 471 · author | holds | Saying that a prince struck coins or built a wall by command still depends on recognizing the direct workers as the actual performers.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · مجاهد والكلبي ومقاتل | reports | Mujahid, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil say God formed each person in a likeness of a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report says that when semen settles in the womb, every vein between it and Adam is brought forth, then the Prophet recited this verse.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p356#2/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farraʾ offers another reading: God could form a person as a human, a beast, or another animal.

NATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r11] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | تركيب means composing and joining one thing to another.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · خارجة عن نافع | reports | Kharija reports Nafiʿ’s reading ركبك كلا with assimilation of one kāf into another.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · جمهور | reports | The majority attach في to ركبك, covering ugly or beautiful, deformed or sound forms.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · بعض المتأولين | reports | Some attach it to عدلك, meaning God formed the human into any image.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · بعض المتأولين | reports | Another view makes it a threat: God could form the human as a donkey, pig, or other creature.
[TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · النبي | reports | In a report transmitted through al-Rida and his forefathers, the Prophet tells a man that the child may resemble any lineage between the sperm and Adam, in accordance with God's forming in whatever image He wills.
[TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · عكرمة وأبو صالح | reports | Ikrima and Abu Salih say God may form a person in any created shape, even a human, donkey, or ape.
[TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · الصادق | reports | Al-Sadiq says God could have formed a person differently but made him in the best form, unlike any animal.
[TABRISI:82:1-19#3/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | A further interpretation lists possible forms by sex, build, beauty, and height: male or female, stout or thin, handsome or ugly, tall or short.
[TABRISI:82:1-19/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | In one grammatical analysis, ma is emphatic and the meaning is that God formed the person in whichever form He chose, tall, short, or otherwise; rakabaka is coordinated with ʿadalaka with a conjunction omitted.
[TABRISI:82:1-19/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | Alternatively, ma is conditional: God formed the person in whatever form He wished; the interrogative phrase must attach to an omitted verb, not rakabaka or ʿadalaka, following Sibawayhi's rule about moving an object before a conditional clause.
[QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · النبي عن موسى بن علي عن أبيه عن جده | reports | Musa ibn Ali reports through his father and grandfather that the Prophet said that, once the sperm settles in the womb, God brings forth every lineage between that person and Adam, in connection with “in whatever image He wished, He composed you.”
[QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · عكرمة وأبو صالح | reports | Ikrima and Abu Salih say God may compose a person in a human, donkey, ape, or pig form.
[QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مكحول | reports | Makhul says the form may be male or female, as God wills.
[QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says the image is a likeness inherited from a father, mother, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, or another relative.
[QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The preposition “fi” attaches to rakkabaka, not ʿadalaka; on the light reading one says ʿadaltu ila, not ʿadaltu fi. Al-Farra therefore rejected that reading when he attached “fi” to ʿadalaka.
[QURTUBI-FULL:82:7-9/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Mā may be an emphatic extra particle, yielding “in whatever image He wished”; alternatively it is conditional, allowing the image of an animal as well as a human.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | The phrase means God formed the person in whichever form He chose; ma may be extra or conditional, with rakabaka as its answer.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The prepositional phrase attaches to adalaka.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:82:7-9/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | This sentence explains the preceding word adalaka, which is why it is not coordinated with the preceding sentence.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | One analysis attaches في أي صورة to ركبك, treats ما as extra, and makes شاء an adjective of صورة; ركبك explains فعدلك rather than joining it with a فاء.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r10] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The passage yields three analyses of ما: extra, conditional with an omitted answer, or accusative as a verbal noun.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | On that analysis, God placed the person in the form his will specified, across such dimensions as beauty, ugliness, height, shortness, and sex.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A second analysis treats the prepositional phrase as a circumstantial phrase attached to an omitted element: he assembled you present in one of the forms.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | A third reported analysis attaches في أي صورة to عدلك, but the author objects that interrogative أي must lead its clause and cannot have a preceding governor.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | Al-Zamakhshari senses wonder in أي, glossing the phrase as God proportioned the person in a wondrous form; the author says this still does not license a preceding governor.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The correct grammatical position is that even interrogative forms used for confirmation cannot have their governor precede them; the same restriction applies to the resembling exclamatory كيف and أنى and to كم الخبرية.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | If في أي صورة attaches to عدلك, ما is accusative with شاء, apparently as a verbal noun: God assembled you as he willed, in a fine arrangement.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqa allows ما to be extra or conditional; either way the clause modifies صورة with an omitted return pronoun (ركبك عليها), and في attaches to ركبك.
[SAMIN-DURR:82:8/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Another view gives the clause no syntactic position because في attaches to one of the two verbs, شاء or ركبك; the interrogative precedes ما, its proper position.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says the form may resemble any of the child’s paternal or maternal relatives: father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report says God brings together in the womb the lineages between the child and Adam, explaining why resemblance is not limited to either parent; Ibn Kathir says it would settle the verse if sound.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Ibn Kathir says this report’s isnad is not established: Mutahhar ibn al-Haytham was called matruk by Abu Sa‘id ibn Yunus, and Ibn Hibban criticized his reports.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | In a report from Abu Hurayra in both Ṣaḥīḥs, a man asks about his dark-skinned newborn; the Prophet compares it to a camel whose color reflects an ancestral trait, suggesting a bloodline cause.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عكرمة | reports | Ikrima says God could form a person in the likeness of an ape or a pig.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو صالح | reports | Abu Ṣāliḥ says God could form a person like a dog, donkey, or pig.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Ibn Kathir reads these reports as showing God’s power to make the embryo a hideous animal, while by power, gentleness, and forbearance He forms it upright, balanced, complete, and beautiful.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p343/r8] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · قتادة | reports | Qatada’s point is that God is fully capable of forming the embryo in such an unusual animal shape.
[BURHAN:v1p429#2/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Sīn in ‘sūra’ marks something that encloses an object from outside, while ṣād in ‘ṣūra’ marks what contains it within.
[NASHR:v1p301/r1] NASHR, d. 833 · أبو الطيب وابن مقسم عن التمار عن رويس | reports | Abu al-Tayyib and Ibn Muqsim, both transmitting through al-Tammar from Ruways, pronounce the preceding assimilation case clearly rather than assimilating it.
[NASHR:v1p301/r2] NASHR, d. 833 · author | reports | The text lists fourteen places of Ruways's optional assimilation: three in al-Baqara, then examples in al-Araf, al-Kahf, Maryam, Taha, al-Naml, al-Zumar, al-Rum, al-Shura, al-Najm, and al-Infitar. | mentions 2:79, 2:175, 3:3, 3:4, 7:41, 6:115, 19:17, 20:39, 27:60, 39:6, 30:42, 42:11, 53:43, 53:44, 82:8, 82:9
[NASHR:v1p302/r3] NASHR, d. 833 · الأهوازي عن رويس | reports | Al-Ahwazi reports Ruways assimilating rakibka kalla; al-Mabhaj includes this reading.
[NASHR:v1p302/r4] NASHR, d. 833 · الباقون عن رويس | reports | Other transmitters from Ruways show all these passages; both assimilation and clear pronunciation are sound transmissions from him. | mentions 2:79, 2:175, 3:3, 3:4, 7:41, 6:115, 19:17, 20:39, 27:60, 39:6, 30:42, 42:11, 53:43, 53:44, 82:8, 82:9

[BIQAI-FULL:v8p350#s082/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report from Mālik b. al-Ḥuwayrith says that at conception the man’s fluid spreads through the woman’s veins and nerves; on the seventh day God gathers every vein reaching back to Adam and recites this verse.  God brings forth ancestral lines to Adam and fashions the child, then the Prophet recites the verse.

[ITQAN:v2p494#3/r4] ITQAN, d. 911 · ابن هشام | rejects | Ibn Hisham objects that rebuke is not apparent in the fashioning verse, the standing of people, or “then its explanation is upon Us”; proposed rebukes are strained, especially after the long separation in the third example.
[ITQAN:v4p534#2/r1] ITQAN, d. 911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A weak-chain report says the Prophet corrected a father who guessed whether a child would resemble either parent: after the sperm settles, God establishes the lineages reaching back to Adam; he glossed ‘in whatever form He willed’ as ‘He shaped you.’
[ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The report’s third implication is that God’s will, not nature, is the effective agent in hereditary traits.
[ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r2] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Remote ancestors’ traits can prevail over those of parents, showing God’s will governs varied natures and forms; hereditary values exist and matter, but judgment rests solely with God.
[ELMALILI:82:8-19#2/r3] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | One should seek nearness to God through faith, gratitude, obedience, and good works, earning future worthiness and protection from punishment rather than presuming on grace.
[ELMALILI:82:8-19/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | reports | One parsing makes rakabaka depend on fi ayyi sura, treats ayyi as an adjective meaning ‘any,’ ma as emphatic, and sha’a as describing sura; it renders God as forming a person in whichever form He wills.
[ELMALILI:82:8-19/r2] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | reports | A second parsing makes ayyi conditional and rakabaka future: God may form a person in any shape or remove him from human beauty into the ugliest forms, warning against delusion.
